### What Booksy does better

- A single flat price — £40 plus £5 a head is easy to work out before you talk to anyone. We publish a range because the products are modular.
- A consumer app that brings new clients — Their marketplace has a large user base. We have none. If discovery is what you need, that matters.

### Where Daviana is different

- No commission layer at all — There is no version of us that takes a share of a client's first visit, because there is no marketplace to source them from.
- Colour is the thing we do that nobody else here does natively — Weighing the bowl and costing it to the gram, onto the client record, is built in rather than bought in.
- The phone — A voice that answers, knows your prices, and writes into the diary the desk is looking at.

### Questions about Booksy and Daviana

#### What does Booksy cost in the UK?

£40 a month for a single user plus £5 a month for each additional team member, plus VAT, per their UK pricing page. Boost, the new-client visibility layer, is separate and charges 30% of a new client’s first visit with a £5 minimum.

#### Do I have to pay Booksy commission?

Only if you switch Boost on. A basic listing is included without commission, and direct bookings are not charged. Worth knowing: turning Boost off does not cancel charges already triggered.

#### Does Booksy handle colour formulas?

There are client notes, as in most systems, but no weighing or gram-costing feature appears in their published feature list. If colour cost is the number you are chasing, notes will not get you there — only a scale will.

## Daviana vs SalonIQ

Source: https://daviana.app/compare/daviana-vs-saloniq/
Published: 2026-09-26  ·  Updated: 2026-09-26

SalonIQ and Daviana are both UK salon software where clients book through your own website and social media, and both now answer the phone with AI. The honest comparison is SalonIQ's marketing tools, larger customer base and lower solo price against a monthly contract, colour costing built in, and one shared record for the diary, the till, the colour bowl and the phone.

Written by Daviana. Every SalonIQ fact below is sourced and dated, checked 2026-09-26. We have tried to be fair; if anything here is out of date, tell us and we will correct it.

### SalonIQ suits you if

You want automated SMS and email marketing in the plan, the reassurance of a system thousands of UK salons already use, or the lowest price for a solo stylist, and a 12-month initial term is fine for you.

### Daviana suits you if

You want a monthly contract you can stop any month, colour weighed and costed without a second supplier, and an AI receptionist with a published price, all on the same client record.

### Side by side

Superscripts link to the source at the foot of the page.

|  | Daviana | SalonIQ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly price | £80 a month including VAT for the diary and till. First month free. | From £47 a month for a solo stylist, every plan with the full booking, management and marketing system. |
| Setup | We set your salon up with you and move your clients and prices across. | One-time setup fee from £175 plus VAT: installation, online training and data migration. |
| Minimum term | None. You can stop any month. | Terms: an initial term of 12 months, then 90 days' written notice. Its UK page says "no long contracts". |
| AI receptionist | Aria, £60 a month including VAT. Books into the Daviana diary. | IQ Connect, powered by Callpad.ai, books into the live SalonIQ diary. Price not published. |
| Colour weighed and costed | ColorLab, built in, £80 a month including VAT. | Through an integration with Vish, a separate system with its own scale and subscription. |
| Marketing campaigns | No bulk SMS or email campaigns today. | Automated SMS and email campaigns in every plan. |
| Salon groups | Built for a group: each salon on its own or the whole group together. | Group dashboards and shared client data; used by 180+ UK salon groups. |
| Upgrades | Bar and Performance included with the diary. | Two-way SMS, a branded client app, online deposits and payments, an e-shop and integrated card payments listed as upgrades. |

### What SalonIQ does better

- Marketing we do not have. Automated SMS and email campaigns come in every SalonIQ plan. Daviana does not run bulk marketing campaigns today.
- A much larger UK customer base. SalonIQ says it powers more than 2,500 UK salons, including 180+ salon groups. Daviana runs in six working salons.
- A lower entry price for a solo stylist. £47 a month against £80, before setup fees and upgrades.
- More add-ons. A branded client app, an e-shop and onsite training are available if you want them.

### Where Daviana is different

- Monthly, with no minimum term. No 12-month initial term and no 90 days' notice. You can stop any month.
- Colour costing built in. ColorLab weighs and costs colour on the same record as the diary and till, without a second supplier or subscription.
- A published price for the AI receptionist. Aria is £60 a month including VAT, and books multi-service visits, such as nails while the colour develops, as one booking.
- One record for everything. The diary, the till, the colour bowl and the phone all read and write the same client record.

### How to compare the price for your salon

Ask SalonIQ for a quote for your team size with the upgrades you would actually use, such as online deposits and card payments, and add the setup fee. Because its terms set a 12-month initial term, compare a full year: 12 months of SalonIQ plus setup, against 12 months of Daviana at £80 a month including VAT, plus £60 for the AI Receptionist or £80 for ColorLab if you want them. If the phone or colour is part of the decision, the missed call calculator and the colour cost calculator show whether either would pay for itself. For the wider market, see our UK salon software comparison.

### Questions about SalonIQ and Daviana

#### How much does SalonIQ cost?

SalonIQ's pricing page says it starts at £47 a month for a solo stylist, with every plan including the complete booking, management and marketing system, plus a one-time setup fee from £175 plus VAT covering installation, training and data migration. Onsite training, two-way SMS, a branded consumer app, online booking deposits and payments, an e-shop and integrated card payments are listed as upgrade options. Daviana's diary and till are £80 a month including VAT.

#### Is SalonIQ a contract?

Check before you sign. SalonIQ's UK page says there are no long contracts, but its published terms and conditions define an initial term of 12 months, after which the contract continues until you give at least 90 days' written notice. Ask SalonIQ which applies to your plan. Daviana has no minimum term: you can stop any month.

#### Does SalonIQ have an AI receptionist?

Yes. SalonIQ's IQ Connect, powered by Callpad.ai, picks up the calls the team cannot take, checks the live SalonIQ diary and books appointments into it. SalonIQ does not publish its price. Daviana's AI Receptionist, Aria, does the same for the Daviana diary at £60 a month including VAT.

#### Does SalonIQ weigh and cost hair colour?

Through an integration. SalonIQ's help centre describes its integration with Vish, a separate colour management system with its own scale and subscription. Daviana's ColorLab is built in, weighs every bowl on a Bluetooth scale and can post the colour charge to the client's bill.

#### Can I move from SalonIQ to Daviana?

Usually, but what moves depends on what you can export. SalonIQ's terms say it deletes or archives customer data 120 days after the contract ends, so export before then. The Daviana team moves your clients and prices across for you.

## Daviana vs Timely

Source: https://daviana.app/compare/daviana-vs-timely/
Published: 2026-09-23  ·  Updated: 2026-09-23

Timely and Daviana are both software with no marketplace, so neither takes a cut of a new client. The honest comparison is Timely's low starting price and marketing tools against colour costing, the phone answered by voice, and one shared record for the whole salon.

Written by Daviana. Every Timely fact below is sourced and dated, checked 2026-09-23. We have tried to be fair; if anything here is out of date, tell us and we will correct it.

### Timely suits you if

You are a small salon or a solo stylist who wants a low weekly price, unlimited team logins, and marketing, loyalty and consultation forms in the same plan.

### Daviana suits you if

Colour cost and the phone are your live problems, you want commission and pay handled without an add-on, and you would rather pay a flat monthly price that does not rise on your busiest weeks.

### Side by side

Superscripts link to the source at the foot of the page.

|  | Daviana | Timely |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly subscription | £80 the diary (Bar and Performance included), £60 the phone answered, £80 colour costed. All inc VAT. Take one, take all three. | From £4, £7 or £9 a week depending on plan, rising with the number of bookings you take each week. Unlimited team members. Advanced team management is +£8 a week. |
| Minimum term | None. We invoice monthly and you can stop any month. | None. No contracts; 14 days' notice to cancel. |
| Marketplace | No | No. Timely describes its pricing as having no new client fees. |
| Card processing | Through the Daviana till | 1.59% + 5p in the salon, 1.85% + 30p online, 3.00% + 30p for international cards |
| Colour weighed and costed to the gram | Yes, built in | No colour-weighing or gram-costing feature found in their published plan comparison |
| The phone answered by AI | Yes. Answers by voice and books into the same diary | No voice receptionist of its own found. Their AI tool, Textie Bestie, helps write SMS messages. |
| Stock | Deducted at the point of use, every gram weighed out of the tube | Retail and professional stock management on Boost and Thrive; the Stock app connects to Timely on Thrive only |
| Team performance and targets | Performance app included: live takings, leaderboards, commission and self-employed settlement | Team performance dashboard, targets and tiered pricing are in the paid add-on on every plan |
| Marketing and loyalty | No bulk SMS campaigns or loyalty scheme today | SMS campaigns, promo codes and loyalty rewards on Boost; rebooking reminders and advanced rewards on Thrive |

### What Timely does better

- A lower starting price for a quiet column. From £4 a week with unlimited team members is hard to beat for a small salon or a single chair. Our Diary alone is £80 a month.
- Marketing and loyalty tools we do not have. SMS campaigns, promo codes, loyalty rewards, review requests and rebooking reminders are all in their plans. We do not run marketing campaigns or a loyalty scheme today.
- Consultation forms and before-and-after photos. Digital consultation forms, sent automatically on Thrive, and photos on the client record. If your treatment menu depends on consultations, that depth counts.
- A long track record. Timely launched in 2011 and is part of EverCommerce. It says more than 28,000 hair and beauty businesses use it.

### Where Daviana is different

- Colour costing is ours, not a note. Weighing the bowl on a Bluetooth scale and costing it to the gram, onto the client's bill, is what ColorLab was built for. A formula in a note tells you what was used; a scale tells you what it cost.
- The phone answered by voice, into the same diary. Callers talk to a receptionist that knows your prices and books into the diary the desk is looking at. No separate company, no link texted to the caller.
- A flat monthly price, not a booking count. Our price does not move with how busy you are. A record Saturday costs the same as a quiet Tuesday.
- Team pay without an add-on. Commission, self-employed settlement and live leaderboards come with the Diary in the Performance app, rather than as a paid extra.

### How to compare the price for your salon

Timely's weekly price starts at £4, £7 or £9 and adjusts with the number of bookings you take, so the figure on the page is a floor. To compare like for like: enter your average weekly bookings on their pricing page, multiply the weekly figure by 52 and divide by 12 for a monthly number, add £8 a week if you want their team performance add-on, then set that against £80 a month for our Diary. As a guide, £4 a week works out at about £17 a month and £9 a week at about £39 a month, before booking volume is added. If colour or the phone is part of the decision, try our colour cost calculator or missed call calculator first; they show whether ColorLab or the AI Receptionist would pay for itself.

### Questions about Timely and Daviana

#### How much does Timely cost in the UK?

Timely's UK pricing page lists three plans starting from £4, £7 and £9 a week (Run, Boost and Thrive), with unlimited team members on every plan. The weekly bill adjusts with the number of bookings you take, so the starting figure is the floor rather than the price a busy salon pays. Advanced team management is an extra £8 a week, and card payments carry processing fees of 1.59% + 5p in the salon and 1.85% + 30p online. Enter your own average weekly bookings on their site to get your real figure.

#### Am I tied in with Timely?

No. Their pricing page says there are no contracts and that you cancel by giving 14 days' notice. Daviana has no minimum term either: we invoice monthly and you can stop any month.

#### Does Timely have an AI receptionist that answers the phone?

Not as a voice product of its own, based on what Timely publishes. Its AI tool, Textie Bestie, helps you write SMS messages to clients. Third-party voice receptionists advertise integrations with Timely, which means a separate company and subscription. Daviana's AI Receptionist answers the call by voice and books into the same diary the front desk uses.

#### Does Timely weigh and cost hair colour?

We found no colour-weighing or gram-costing feature in Timely's published pricing and feature table. It has client notes, consultation forms and before-and-after photos on its Boost and Thrive plans, which record a formula but do not cost it. Daviana's ColorLab weighs every bowl on a Bluetooth scale and costs it to the gram onto the client's bill.

## Daviana ColorLab vs Vish

Source: https://daviana.app/compare/daviana-vs-vish/
Published: 2026-09-26  ·  Updated: 2026-09-26

Vish and Daviana ColorLab are both hair colour management software: a Bluetooth scale at the colour bar, the formula saved to the client, and the cost of the bowl in front of you. The honest difference is where each one lives. Vish plugs into the booking system you already use. ColorLab is part of Daviana, on the same record as the diary and the till.

Written by Daviana. Every Vish fact below is sourced and dated, checked 2026-09-26. We have tried to be fair; if anything here is out of date, tell us and we will correct it.

### Vish suits you if

You are keeping your current booking system, such as Phorest, SalonIQ or Shortcuts, and want colour tracking that plugs into it, or you are a single stylist who wants the lowest monthly starting price.

### ColorLab suits you if

You want colour weighed and costed on the same record as your diary and till, so the colour charge lands on the bill without a sync, with formulas that can start from a photo and a UK price that includes VAT.

### Side by side

Superscripts link to the source at the foot of the page.

|  | Daviana ColorLab | Vish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly price | £80 a month including VAT. First month free, cancel any month. | From $40 a month (Vish Solo) to $365 (Vish 20); Enterprise on quote. Listed in US dollars, subject to local taxes. |
| Scales and devices | A Bluetooth precision scale guides every pour to the gram. Runs on iOS and the web. | Scales are extra at $195 each. You provide a tablet (iPad or Android) for each scale. |
| Setup | We set your salon up with you and move your clients and prices across. | One-time location setup and education fee, with a customer success rep. |
| Booking system | Part of Daviana. ColorLab reads and writes the same record as the Daviana diary and till. | Connects to your existing salon software, including Phorest, SalonIQ, Shortcuts, Zenoti, Square and Boulevard. |
| Colour charge on the bill | Where a salon turns it on, the colour charge posts back to the appointment. | Exact usage and prices are sent to the front desk. |
| Formula history | Saved to the client for good, across every branch. Last formula reloads in one tap. | Mix from scratch or from stored history; formulas saved to the client record in your salon software. |
| Formula from a photo | Yes. Suggests shades and grams from a photo and the client's history, and asks to confirm when unsure. | No photo-to-formula feature found on the pages we checked. |
| Leftover colour | Stock comes off by what was actually poured. | A reweigh step subtracts leftovers from the recorded formula. |

### What Vish does better

- It works with the booking system you already have. Vish lists integrations with Phorest, SalonIQ, Shortcuts, Zenoti, Square, Boulevard and more. If you are not moving your diary, Vish slots in beside it. ColorLab's cost-to-bill link is with Daviana.
- A cheaper start for one stylist. Vish Solo is $40 a month. ColorLab is £80, so for a single chair Vish costs less before hardware.
- Android tablets. Vish runs on an iPad or an Android tablet. ColorLab runs on iOS and the web.
- The reweigh step. Weighing what is left in the bowl after the service and taking it off the formula is a neat habit Vish builds in.

### Where ColorLab is different

- One record, not a sync. ColorLab reads the day's colour clients, their history and per-stylist pricing straight from Daviana Diary, and writes the cost back. There is no second system to keep in step.
- A formula can start from a photo. Photograph the hair and ColorLab suggests shades and grams from the photo and the client's colour history, with safety rules that ask to confirm rather than guess.
- A UK price, VAT included. £80 a month including VAT, first month free, cancel any month.
- The rest of the salon in the same system. The same record also runs the diary and till, and the AI Receptionist books calls into it.

### How to compare the price for your salon

Vish prices in US dollars by plan, and scales ($195 each), a tablet per scale and a one-time setup fee sit on top. To compare like for like, pick the Vish plan that fits your team, convert it to pounds, add local tax, then add the scales and tablets you need. Set that against £80 a month including VAT for ColorLab. Before either, work out what a head of colour costs you today with our free colour cost calculator: that is the number colour management software is meant to bring down. More on the problem itself in how much hair colour is your salon really wasting?

### Questions about Vish and ColorLab

#### How much does Vish cost?

Vish's pricing page lists plans in US dollars: Vish Solo $40 a month, Vish Starter $100, Vish 5 $215, Vish 10 $290 and Vish 20 $365, with Enterprise on quote. Scales are not included in the subscription and cost $195 each, you provide a tablet (iPad or Android) for each scale, and there is a one-time location setup and education fee. Prices are subject to local taxes. We found no pound sterling price on the page. Daviana ColorLab is £80 a month including VAT.

#### Is Daviana ColorLab a Vish alternative for UK salons?

Yes, both weigh the colour bowl on a Bluetooth scale, save the formula to the client and show what the colour cost. The main difference is where they sit. Vish connects to the booking system you already use. ColorLab is part of Daviana, so it reads and writes the same client record as the Daviana diary and till, and where a salon turns it on the colour charge posts to the client's bill.

#### Does Vish work with Phorest?

Yes. Vish lists Phorest among its integrations, alongside SalonIQ, Shortcuts, Zenoti, Square and Boulevard, and offers a paid Sync+ add-on for Phorest salons on its Vish 5, 10 and 20 plans ($50, $75 and $100 a month). If you are staying on one of those systems, that is a real point in Vish's favour.

#### Can ColorLab suggest a colour formula?

Yes. Photograph the hair and ColorLab reads it together with the client's colour history, then suggests the shades and grams. Where it is not sure, its safety rules ask the stylist to confirm rather than guess. A returning client's last formula reloads in one tap.

#### Which one is cheaper?

It depends on your team size and whether you already use Daviana. Vish Solo at $40 a month is cheaper than ColorLab for a single stylist, before scales, tablets and the setup fee. For a salon, compare the Vish plan that fits your team, plus scales and tablets, against ColorLab at £80 a month including VAT. Our free colour cost calculator shows what a head of colour costs you today, which is the number either tool is meant to reduce.

### Sources

- Vish: pricing (plans, scales, tablets, setup and education fee, Sync+ for Phorest) — checked 2026-09-26
- Vish: integrations (salon software it connects to, what syncs) — checked 2026-09-26
- Vish: how it works (select and mix, reweigh, charge, track; customer success setup) — checked 2026-09-26

## Fresha alternatives for UK salons

Source: https://daviana.app/compare/fresha-alternatives/
Published: 2026-09-26  ·  Updated: 2026-09-26

Fresha's software is cheap, and its marketplace brings new clients. The costs sit elsewhere: a 20% one-time commission on each new marketplace client, card fees on every payment, and texts beyond the free allowance. Most salons looking for an alternative want one of two things: no marketplace at all, or a price that does not grow with every new client. Here are five UK options, with where each one wins.

Written by Daviana, one of the options below. Every fact about another company is sourced and dated, checked 2026-09-26. If anything here is out of date, tell us and we will correct it.

### Fresha alternatives side by side

Superscripts link to the sources at the foot of the page.

|  | Price | Contract and new-client fee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresha (for reference) | £14.95 a month on your own; £9.95 a month per bookable team member on Team | Contract: None; cancel any timeNew clients: 20% one-time commission on new marketplace clients, minimum £4 |
| Timely | From £4, £7 or £9 a week by plan, adjusting with the bookings you take; unlimited team members | Contract: None; 14 days' noticeNew clients: No new client fees |
| Booksy | £40 a month plus £5 a month per extra team member, plus VAT | Contract: None; cancel any timeNew clients: Only if you turn on Boost: 30% of a new client's first visit, minimum £5 |
| SalonIQ | From £47 a month for a solo stylist; setup fee from £175 plus VAT | Contract: 12-month initial term, then 90 days' written notice, per its termsNew clients: No marketplace |
| Phorest | Quote only; no free trial | Contract: One year, auto-renewing; two months' notice before the anniversaryNew clients: No marketplace |
| Daviana | £80 a month including VAT for the diary and till; first month free | Contract: None; cancel any monthNew clients: None. No marketplace and no commission on bookings |

### The alternatives, one by one

- Timely. The lowest published starting price, from £4 a week with unlimited team members, and no new client fees. The weekly price adjusts with how many bookings you take, so enter your own numbers on their site. See Daviana vs Timely.
- Booksy. Still a consumer marketplace, but on a flat £40 a month plus £5 per extra team member (plus VAT), and new-client commission only when you switch Boost on. The closest to Fresha if you want to keep being found in an app. See Daviana vs Booksy.
- SalonIQ. UK salon software from £47 a month for a solo stylist, with a setup fee from £175 plus VAT and no marketplace. Its terms set a 12-month initial term, then 90 days' written notice, so ask before signing. See Daviana vs SalonIQ.
- Phorest. A long-established system for larger salons, priced by quote, on a one-year contract that renews automatically unless you give two months' notice. See Daviana vs Phorest.
- Daviana. A salon booking system and till at £80 a month including VAT, with no marketplace, no commission and no minimum term. It costs more than Fresha for a small team. It fits salons that also want colour weighed and costed with ColorLab and the phone answered by an AI receptionist, all on the same client record. See Daviana vs Fresha.

### What Fresha still does better

- New clients. Fresha says its marketplace has more than 25 million customers looking to book. None of the no-marketplace options replaces that.
- A low software price. £14.95 a month on your own is cheaper than most of the list.
- No contract. You can leave any month, so there is no lock-in to escape.

### How to choose

Take your last three months on Fresha and add up four things: the subscription, the marketplace commission you paid, card processing, and paid texts. Then look at how many of those months' bookings came from the marketplace, not from regulars. If the marketplace is bringing clients who stay, the commission may be worth it. If most of your diary is regulars, you are paying for reach you do not need, and a flat-price system without a marketplace is likely to cost less. Our 12 questions to ask before switching salon software covers the rest.

### Questions about leaving Fresha

#### What is the cheapest alternative to Fresha in the UK?

On published prices, Timely starts lowest at £4 a week, with unlimited team members, though its weekly price adjusts with the number of bookings you take. Fresha itself is £14.95 a month on your own, so for a solo stylist who is happy with the marketplace, staying may be cheapest.

#### Is there a Fresha alternative with no commission on new clients?

Yes. Timely says it has no new client fees. SalonIQ, Phorest and Daviana have no marketplace, so there is nothing to take a commission on. Booksy only charges a one-time 30% (minimum £5) on new clients who book while its optional Boost feature is switched on.

#### Which Fresha alternatives have no contract?

Timely (14 days' notice), Booksy (cancel any time) and Daviana (cancel any month) have no minimum term. Phorest's UK terms are a one-year contract that renews automatically unless you give two months' notice. SalonIQ's terms set a 12-month initial term, then 90 days' written notice, although its UK page says "no long contracts", so ask which applies.

#### Can I move my clients from Fresha to another system?

Usually, but what moves depends on what you can export from Fresha. Before you switch, ask any new supplier to look at a real export: client details, appointment history and notes. The Daviana team moves your clients and prices across for you.

#### Is Fresha still worth it?

For many salons, yes. If new clients from the marketplace are worth more to you than the 20% one-time fee, and you are happy with the payment rates, Fresha's software price is hard to beat. The case for switching is strongest when most of your bookings are regulars.

Phorest's UK terms say that if you terminate before the end of the contracted period you owe the subscription fees for the rest of it. Check your renewal date and give written notice at least two months before it if you plan to move.

SalonIQ is the closest like-for-like: UK salon software with marketing tools and no marketplace. Daviana is also a no-marketplace system, with colour costing and an AI receptionist on the same record. Fresha and Booksy are cheaper to start but are built around a consumer marketplace.

#### Is Phorest still worth it?

For many larger salons, yes. It has a long track record across many sites and a large support team. The case for moving is strongest if the contract or a quoted price no longer suits you.

## Treatwell alternatives for UK salons

Source: https://daviana.app/compare/treatwell-alternatives/
Published: 2026-09-30  ·  Updated: 2026-09-30

The main Treatwell alternatives for UK salons are Fresha and Booksy if you still want a consumer marketplace at a lower commission, and Timely, SalonIQ or Daviana if you would rather pay a flat price and no commission. Treatwell itself suits a salon with empty columns: it takes 35% plus VAT of a new marketplace client's first booking and nothing on repeat visits. Salons usually look elsewhere once the diary is full of regulars and that first-booking fee stops paying for itself. Here is where each alternative wins.

Written by Daviana, one of the options below. Every fact about another company is sourced and dated; all seven sources were re-checked 2026-09-30. If anything here is out of date, tell us and we will correct it.

### Treatwell alternatives side by side

Superscripts link to the sources at the foot of the page.

|  | Price | Contract and new-client fee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Treatwell (for reference) | Monthly fee not published on its pricing page | Contract: 30 days' notice, per its partner termsNew clients: 35% commission on a new marketplace client's first booking; 0% on repeat bookings; 2.5% on online prepayments; all plus VAT |
| Fresha | £14.95 a month on your own; £9.95 a month per bookable team member on Team | Contract: None; cancel any timeNew clients: 20% one-time commission on new marketplace clients, minimum £4 |
| Booksy | £40 a month plus £5 a month per extra team member, plus VAT; 7-day free trial | Contract: None; cancel any timeNew clients: Only with Boost on: 30% of a new client's first visit, minimum £5, plus VAT |
| Timely | From £4, £7 or £9 a week by plan, adjusting with the bookings you take; unlimited team members | Contract: None; 14 days' noticeNew clients: No new client fees |
| SalonIQ | From £47 a month for a solo stylist; setup fee from £175 plus VAT | Contract: Its pricing page says no long-term contracts and 60 days' notice; its terms set a 12-month initial term, then 90 days' written noticeNew clients: No marketplace |
| Daviana | £80 a month including VAT for the diary and till; first month free | Contract: None; cancel any monthNew clients: None. No marketplace and no commission on bookings |

### The alternatives, one by one

- Fresha. The closest swap if you still want marketplace clients: a one-time 20% on new marketplace clients (minimum £4) against Treatwell's 35%, with a published price of £14.95 a month on your own or £9.95 per bookable team member and no contract. See Daviana vs Fresha.
- Booksy. A marketplace where the commission is a switch. Marketplace bookings are free while Boost is off; with Boost on it is a one-time 30% of a new client's first visit, minimum £5, plus VAT. The subscription is £40 a month plus £5 per extra team member, plus VAT. See Daviana vs Booksy.
- Timely. No marketplace and no new client fees, from £4 a week with unlimited team members and 14 days' notice to leave. The weekly price adjusts with bookings, so enter your own numbers on their site. See Daviana vs Timely.
- SalonIQ. UK salon software with marketing tools and no marketplace, from £47 a month for a solo stylist plus a setup fee. Its pricing page and its terms describe the commitment differently, so ask which applies to you before signing. See Daviana vs SalonIQ.
- Daviana. A salon booking system and till at £80 a month including VAT, with no marketplace, no commission and no minimum term. It will not send you new clients the way Treatwell does. It fits salons that are busy enough already and also want colour weighed and costed with ColorLab and the phone answered by an AI receptionist, all on the same client record. See Daviana vs Treatwell.

### What Treatwell still does better

- You pay when a new client books. The commission only applies to first bookings from new marketplace clients, and repeat bookings are 0%. For a salon with quiet columns and no marketing budget, that is a lower-risk shape than a subscription with no clients attached.
- Direct bookings stay commission-free. Calls, texts, clients you add yourself and bookings through the Book Now button on your website and social media carry no commission.
- Reach. A consumer marketplace people already search. None of the no-marketplace options on this page replaces that.
- Short notice. You can leave on 30 days' notice, per its partner terms.

### How to choose

Start with what Treatwell actually cost you last month, not the 35% headline. Take your own numbers:

- Commission. The number of new marketplace clients times their average first-booking price times 35%, plus VAT. Say 8 new clients at £60: 8 × £21 = £168, or £201.60 with VAT.
- Prepayment fee. 2.5% plus VAT on anything clients paid online in advance. On £1,000 of prepaid bookings that is £25, or £30 with VAT.
- Monthly fee. Whatever is on your own invoice, since Treatwell does not publish it.

In that example the month comes to £231.60 before the monthly fee, and most of it is commission. The numbers are only an illustration, so use your own. Now ask how many of those eight clients came back. If most of them did, Treatwell is earning its fee, and the question is whether Fresha at 20% or Booksy with Boost would bring the same people for less. If your diary is full of regulars and few new faces come from the marketplace, you are mostly paying for a diary, and a no-marketplace system may do more for the money. Some salons keep a marketplace listing for new clients and run the salon on something else; if you do, make sure you do not end up with two diaries. Our 12 questions to ask before switching salon software covers the rest, and the UK salon software guide compares the wider field.

### Questions about leaving Treatwell

#### Why do salons look for a Treatwell alternative?

Usually because of the commission. Treatwell charges 35% plus VAT on the first booking of each new client it brings from its marketplace, which is 42% of that appointment once VAT is added. Salons with a full diary of regulars often decide they no longer need to buy new clients at that price, and want software that is not built around a marketplace.

#### How much commission does Treatwell take?

Treatwell's UK pricing page says 35% on first bookings made by new clients it brings from the marketplace, 0% on repeat bookings, and a 2.5% processing fee on online prepayments. All commissions and fees are subject to VAT. Bookings made directly with you, or through the Book Now button on your website and social media, carry no commission.

#### Does Treatwell charge a monthly fee?

Its pricing page refers to a monthly fee but does not publish the amount for either the Freelancer or the Advanced plan, so ask for it in writing before you compare. The alternatives on this page all publish their prices.

#### Which Treatwell alternative has the lowest commission?

Timely, SalonIQ and Daviana have no marketplace, so they charge no commission on new clients at all. Of the marketplaces, Fresha charges a one-time 20% with a £4 minimum, and Booksy charges 30% with a £5 minimum plus VAT, and only while its Boost feature is switched on.

#### Do I keep my clients if I leave Treatwell?

Treatwell's pricing page says the data remains the property of your establishment, including if you cancel your plan, and its partner terms let you leave on 30 days' notice. Ask any new supplier to look at a real export before you sign, including client notes and colour formulas, which are the easiest data to lose. The Daviana team moves your clients and prices across for you.

### Questions about leaving Booksy

Salons that no longer need marketplace clients often want software that is not built around one.

Only when you turn Boost on. Booksy then charges a one-time fee of 30% of the total cost of a new client's first visit, with a minimum of £5, plus VAT. Clients who find you through your own marketing, your Booksy profile link, or the marketplace with Boost switched off carry no commission, according to Booksy's UK pricing page.

#### Is Booksy's £40 a month including VAT?

No. Booksy's UK pricing page says VAT is added to the final price, so the subscription is £48 a month for one person, plus £6 a month for each extra team member once VAT is added.

#### Which Booksy alternative is cheapest?

On published prices for a small team, Fresha (£14.95 a month on your own) and Timely (from £4 a week) start lowest. Fresha charges a one-time 20% fee on new marketplace clients, minimum £4, while Timely has no new client fees. Run your own team size and bookings through each one before deciding.

#### Can I move my clients from Booksy?

# Questions about Daviana

---

## Questions about Daviana Diary, the salon booking system

Source: https://daviana.app/diary/

### What is a salon booking system?

It is the diary a salon runs on: appointments by stylist, the till and the client record. Daviana's salon booking system keeps the appointment diary, till, client records, per-stylist pricing, rota and online booking in one system, so nothing is typed in twice.

### How much does Daviana's booking system cost?

£80 a month including VAT. There is no commission and no charge per booking, the first month is free, and you can cancel any month. Bar and Performance are included with it. See pricing.

### Can clients book online?

Yes. Make a service bookable online and clients book themselves into the same diary from your own branded page, with a deposit taken at booking. Opening hours and each stylist's rota decide which slots are offered, so online booking can never sell a slot that is not really there.

### Do you take commission on bookings?

No. You pay a monthly subscription and that is it. We do not take a cut of your takings, we do not charge per booking, and we do not market your clients to other salons. Your client list is yours.

### Can I move across from Phorest, Fresha or another system?

Yes. The Daviana team helps move your clients and prices across. What can be moved depends on what your current system lets you export, so we look at your data on the demo and plan the changeover around your quietest week. Our honest comparisons with Phorest and Fresha say where each one wins.

### Does it work for a salon group?

Yes. It was built for a group, not retrofitted to one. Each salon gets its own diary, and you can see each salon on its own or the whole group together.

### What do I need to run it?

The diary, till and reporting run on what you already have: it works in a web browser and on iOS.

### Is Daviana a good booking system for nail and beauty salons?

Yes. Every team member has their own column, every service books its own length, and eligibility decides who can perform what, so online booking only offers a treatment with people who actually do it. Hair, nails and beauty share one diary, and the AI Receptionist can book a manicure while the colour develops as a single visit.

### Does it work as a salon till and POS?

Yes. You cash out against the appointment: services, retail, tips and payment type land on one bill, attributed to the stylist who did the work, with card, cash and gift card payments. Nothing is re-keyed into a second system.

### How does the price compare with Fresha or Booksy?

On their published UK prices (checked 26 September 2026), Fresha is £14.95 a month on your own or £9.95 per bookable team member, plus 20% on each new marketplace client, and Booksy is £40 a month plus £5 per extra team member, plus VAT. Daviana is £80 a month including VAT with no marketplace and no commission. For a small team Fresha or Booksy costs less; our UK salon software comparison sets out the full picture.

## Questions about Daviana Aria, the AI receptionist

Source: https://daviana.app/ai-receptionist/

### What is an AI receptionist for a hair salon?

An AI receptionist answers the salon phone with a real AI voice when nobody on the desk can. Daviana's, called Aria, handles the whole call: it checks who is free for each service, books the visit straight into the live Daviana diary, and saves a note of the call on the client's record.

### Does it book into my real diary?

Yes, the same diary your front desk is looking at, not a copy it has to reach into from outside. It answers from a live read of the diary, respecting each stylist's rota and breaks, and re-checks the exact slot at the moment of booking. Once it books, the slot is gone for everyone. More in can an AI answer your salon's phone and still book into the real diary?

### Can it book more than one service in a visit?

Yes. It builds a real visit rather than a single slot: nails while the colour develops, two specialists staggered, or a group split across chairs. Every service is checked for who is actually free, then saved as one booking.

### Does it answer out of hours?

Yes. Evenings, Sundays and the middle of your Saturday rush are exactly when calls ring out, and they are the calls least likely to ring back. The missed call calculator shows what those calls are worth to your salon.

### What happens if it does not know the answer?

It takes a message for the team rather than guessing. It never invents a price, and on anything to do with money or fees it leaves the decision to you. Card numbers are blocked before any AI model sees them, and money is never settled on the call.

### Does it speak other languages?

Yes. It can switch language mid-call, and it copes with accents, speakerphone and background noise. There are no menus and no "press 1".

### How much does the AI receptionist cost?

£60 a month including VAT, with the first month free and cancellation any month. It books into Daviana Diary, which is £80 a month. See pricing.

### Can I hear it before I decide?

Yes. Use the call-me form above: Aria reads your salon's website for about thirty seconds, then rings your mobile and answers as your salon. One test call per salon per day, between 8am and 9pm.

### Does Aria work for nail and beauty salons?

Yes. Aria books a whole visit rather than a single slot, so nails while the colour develops, two specialists staggered, or a group split across chairs are booked as one visit. For every service it checks who actually does that treatment and who is free, so a client is never offered someone who does not do it.

## Questions about Daviana ColorLab, hair colour management software

Source: https://daviana.app/colorlab/

### What is hair colour management software?

Hair colour management software measures, records and costs the colour a salon mixes. Daviana ColorLab does it with a Bluetooth precision scale: every bowl is weighed to the gram, the formula is saved to the client's record, and the product cost of the bowl shows the moment it is weighed.

### How does ColorLab cut colour waste?

The scale guides every pour to the gram, so stylists stop over-mixing and the colour that used to go in the bin stays in the bowl. Product used comes off the stock count, so reordering follows what was really poured, not a hunch. There is more on where the waste happens in how much hair colour is your salon really wasting?

### What happens to colour formulas when a stylist leaves?

They stay with the salon. Every formula is saved to the client's record, across every branch, and a returning client's last formula reloads in one tap, whoever is on the chair. We wrote about why formulas get lost when a stylist leaves.

### Can ColorLab suggest a formula?

Yes. Photograph the hair and ColorLab reads it together with the client's colour history, then suggests the shades and grams. Where it is not sure, its safety rules ask the stylist to confirm rather than guess.

### Which colour brands and scale does it use?

The shade picker covers Redken, Keyluma and Organic shades, plus highlights, in one app. Weighing uses an Acaia precision scale connected over Bluetooth, so the weight lands on the client's record without anyone writing it down.

### How much does ColorLab cost?

£80 a month including VAT, with the first month free and cancellation any month. ColorLab reads and writes Daviana Diary, so where a salon turns it on, the colour charge posts to the client's bill. See pricing.

### How do I work out what colour costs my salon today?

Use the free salon colour cost calculator. It works from your own spend, not industry averages, and you do not need to give an email to see the number.

The AI Receptionist, which answers the phone and books into the same diary, is £60 a month. ColorLab, which weighs and costs every colour bowl to the gram, is £80 a month. Bar and Performance are included free once you take the Diary. Take one, take all five. There is no commission on bookings and no lock-in.

### Can I take just one product?

Yes. Each product is priced on its own and works on its own. They share one record, so adding another later means nothing is entered twice and nothing you have already set up is lost.

### Does Daviana charge commission on bookings?

No. Daviana is a monthly subscription. There is no per-booking charge and no commission on takings, and client lists are not marketed to other salons.

## Questions salon owners ask

Source: https://daviana.app/faq/

Straight answers about what Daviana does, what it costs to switch, how your data moves across, and what happens on day one.

### What Daviana actually is

The short version, before the detail.

#### What is Daviana?

Daviana is one connected system that runs a whole hair salon. It covers the appointment diary and till, the phone answered and booked, and colour weighed and costed to the gram. The difference from most salon software is that these are not separate products behind one login — they read and write the same record, so the diary, the colour bowl and the till all agree.

#### Is Daviana one product or several?

Five products, one shared record. Daviana Diary is the booking spine — the diary, till and client record. The AI Receptionist, ColorLab, Bar and Performance all read and write that same record rather than keeping their own copy of your clients. Bar and Performance come included once you take the Diary. You do not have to take all five.

#### Do I have to take all five products?

No. Each is priced on its own and works on its own — Bar and Performance are included once you take the Diary. Most salons start with the diary and add the one thing that is actively hurting — usually the phone or colour cost. Because everything reads the same record, adding a product later does not mean a second set-up or a second copy of your client list.

#### Who is Daviana for?

Hair salons — particularly ones past the point where a single diary app is enough: more than a few chairs, colour work, a mix of employed and self-employed stylists, and a phone that rings more than someone can answer. It is built for salon owners, not for a single mobile stylist.

#### Who builds it?

The same team that runs working salons, from London to Saudi, with partner salons across five countries. Every product was written because something on our own floor was broken. It is used every day in our own chairs before it reaches anyone else’s.

### Money

What it costs, and what it saves.

#### How much does Daviana cost?

It is priced per product, and every price includes VAT. Daviana Diary — the diary, till and client record — is £80 a month. The AI Receptionist is £60 a month. ColorLab is £80 a month. Bar and Performance are included free once you take the Diary. Take one, take all five.

It is a monthly subscription. There is no charge per booking and no commission on your clients. See pricing to tick what you need and see the total.

#### Can I take just one product?

Yes. Each product is priced on its own and works on its own — most salons start with the diary, or with whichever one is costing them money today. They share one record, so adding another later means nothing is entered twice and nothing you have already set up is lost.

#### Do you take a commission on my bookings?

No. You pay a monthly subscription and that is it. We do not take a cut of your takings, we do not charge per booking, and we do not market your clients to other salons. Your client list is yours.

#### Is there a contract or a lock-in?

Your data is yours and you can export it. We would rather you stayed because the system works than because leaving is painful. Exact terms are covered on the demo.

#### What does it cost to add a stylist?

Ask this of any salon system you look at, including ours — pricing that scales per head can change the maths considerably as you grow. We will be straight about how ours works on the call.

#### Will it actually save me money?

The two places salons usually find money are colour and the phone. Colour, because weighing the bowl shows what a head actually costs and where the overmixing is. The phone, because calls that ring out do not show up anywhere as a loss — you simply never hear from that person. Whether those add up to more than the subscription depends on your salon, and we would rather work that out with you on the demo than promise a number here.

### Switching

The part everyone is actually worried about.

#### What happens to my existing client data?

It comes with you. Client records, contact details and appointment history are the things a salon cannot afford to lose, and moving them across is the first thing we deal with — not an afterthought. We will look at exactly what you have on the demo, because what can be moved depends on what your current system will let you export.

#### Will I lose my colour history and client notes?

This is the one to ask hardest, of anyone. Notes and colour history are usually the messiest data in a salon and the easiest to quietly drop in a migration. Bring an example of what your current records look like to the demo and we will tell you honestly what will carry across and what will not.

#### How long does it take to set up?

It depends on the size of the salon and how much history is coming across. What matters more than the number of days is the sequencing — you do not want the changeover landing on a Friday. We plan it around your quietest week.

#### What happens on the first Saturday?

The honest answer is that the first busy day on any new system is the one that hurts, so we plan for it rather than pretend it will not happen. That means the diary being right before you go live, someone reachable on the day, and not moving everything at once.

#### Can I run it alongside my current system for a while?

For some parts, yes — the phone and colour can run before you move the diary, because they add something rather than replace something. Running two diaries at once is the one thing we would talk you out of; that is how double-bookings happen.

### The phone

How the AI Receptionist works in practice.

#### Does the AI receptionist book into my real diary?

Yes — the same diary your front desk is looking at, not a copy it has to reach into from outside. That is the whole point. When it takes a booking, the slot is gone for everyone immediately, so two people cannot be given the same 2pm.

#### What happens if it does not know the answer?

It hands over to a person rather than guessing. It will not invent a price, and it will not promise something the salon does not do. Being straight about what it does not know is more important than sounding clever.

#### Will my clients know it is not a person?

We do not set out to trick anyone. In practice most callers want the same three things — an appointment, a price, or your opening hours — and they care much more about getting them quickly than about who answered. The alternative being compared against is usually voicemail.

#### Does it answer out of hours?

Yes. Evenings, Sundays and the middle of your Saturday rush are exactly when calls ring out, and they are the calls least likely to ring back — most people simply try the next salon.

### Practical things

Hardware, languages, and what happens if something breaks.

#### What hardware do I need?

The diary, till and reporting run on what you already have. Colour weighing needs a scale that talks to the system, so the weight lands on the client’s record without anyone typing it in — if a stylist has to stop and write a number down on a Saturday, it will not happen.

#### Does it work in more than one language?

Yes. It runs across salons from London to Saudi Arabia, and the site itself is in English, Italian, Russian and Spanish. If you need a specific language on the phone or in the app, ask on the demo.

#### Can I use it across more than one salon?

Yes — it was built for a group, not retrofitted to one. You can see each salon on its own and the whole group together, which is usually the thing that is hardest to get out of software designed for a single site.

#### What happens if something goes wrong on a busy day?

You reach the people who build it. We run salons ourselves, so a Saturday going wrong is not an abstract support ticket to us — it is the same day of the week that hurts us.

### The demo

What actually happens if you book one.

#### What happens on the demo?

Thirty minutes, on your numbers rather than ours. Bring your current colour spend, a normal week’s diary and your biggest annoyance. We will show you the parts that touch that problem and skip the rest. There are no slides.

#### Do I need to prepare anything?

It helps if you know roughly what you spend on colour a month and how many calls you think go unanswered — but if you do not know those numbers, that is a useful finding in itself and a fair place to start.

#### Will I be sold to?

We will tell you if we do not think it fits. Salons talk to each other, and a salon that signs up for the wrong reasons leaves within a year and tells people why.
